name.description:
Name of the check in results, unique within the step. Without one,
the check is named after its type, selector, operator and value, and
for every type except header that label contains the expected value
as written; give a check whose value is sensitive a name.

type.description:
What the check reads: "status" (the status code), "header", "body",
"json" (the body as JSON), "html" (the body as HTML), "timing", "url"
(the final URL after redirects; the request URL when redirects are
not followed) or "cookie".

selector.description:
What to read, by type: the header name for header (case-insensitive;
when the header repeats, any of its values may match), a JSON path
such as "$.data.items[0].id" for json, a CSS selector for html, the
cookie name for cookie. Other types take no selector.

in.description: status: the status code is one of these.

not_in.description: status: the status code is none of these.

between.description: status: the status code is within [low, high], both included.

equals.description:
header, body, html, url (a string) and json (a string, number or
true/false): the value is exactly this. For html, the value is the
text content of the first matching element (its text and its
descendants' text, without tags) with leading and trailing white
space trimmed. For json, equality is between scalars only; an object
or array never equals. A string equals a string with the same text,
true/false the same value, and a number a number with the same exact
decimal value (42 equals 42.0 and 4.2e1, with no float64 rounding);
a string never equals a number or true/false.

contains.description:
header, body, url (a non-empty string): the value contains this
text. json (a string, number or true/false): the array contains
this element, compared as equals compares; any other JSON kind
fails the check.

not_contains.description: body: the body does not contain this text.

matches.description:
header, body, url and json: the value matches this regular
expression (RE2 syntax). For json, it applies to string values; any
other JSON kind fails the check.

exists.description:
header, html, cookie and json: the header, element, cookie or path
is present. For cookie, it reads the Set-Cookie headers of this
response. Must be true.

missing.description: json: the path is absent. Must be true.

empty.description: body: the body is empty. Must be true.

is.description:
json: the value at the path is of this JSON kind: "array",
"object", "string", "number", "bool" or "null".

count.description:
json: the array at the path has this many elements, e.g. "> 0". A
value that is not an array fails the check.

size.description: body: the size of the decoded response body in bytes, e.g. "< 50kb".

duration.description:
timing: the total request time, the same measurement the duration
thresholds use, e.g. "< 500ms".

on_fail.description:
What a failure does: "record" counts it toward the check rate only,
"fail" also fails the run, and "abort" fails the run and ends the
virtual user's current iteration after the step's other checks are
evaluated (the test goes on). Defaults: "fail" for status, "record"
for every other type.

Check.description: An assertion on the response: a type, a selector where the type needs one, and exactly one operator.

data_source.description: Name or path of the CSV file.

data_content.description: Base64-encoded content of the CSV file.

has_header.description: The first row holds column names.

mode.description: How virtual users take rows: in order, at random, or each row once.

DataConfig.description: A CSV data source. Each virtual user takes rows according to mode.

variable_name.description: Name of the variable that receives the value.

selector.description:
What to read, by type: a JSON path, a regex, a header name, a cookie
name or a CSS selector.

attribute.description: HTML attribute to read, for type html.

type.description: Where to read the value from.

required.description:
Treat a miss (nothing found) as a failed check labelled
"extract <variable_name>". Required or not, an extractor always
assigns its variable; a miss assigns "".

on_fail.description:
What a miss does when required is true: "record", "fail" or "abort"
(the default). Only applies with required: true.

Extract.description: A value to capture from the response.

weight.description: Relative share of the virtual users.

RegionWeight.description: One cloud region's share of the virtual users.

url.description:
An absolute http(s) URL, a URL starting with ${variable}, or a path
starting with "/" that is appended to target.base_url.

Request.description: An HTTP request. The URL, body and header values may contain ${variable} references.

name.description: Scenario name, unique within the test.

weight.description: Relative chance that a virtual user runs this scenario.

think_time.description: Pause after each run of the scenario, e.g. "1s".

auto_handle_cookies.description: Keep cookies between the steps of a run.

data_config.description: CSV data whose columns fill ${column} variables.

thresholds.description: Pass/fail rules for this scenario, e.g. "iteration_duration_p95 < 5s".

Scenario.description: A sequence of steps that a virtual user runs.

duration.description: How long the stage lasts, e.g. "1m".

target.description: Number of virtual users at the end of the stage.

Stage.description: One stage of a staged load profile.

name.description: Step name, unique within the scenario.

extract.description: Values to capture from the response into ${variable_name}.

checks.description:
Assertions on the response. Each check is reported separately. When
no response is received (a transport error or a timeout), the
step's checks are not evaluated and not counted.

thresholds.description: Pass/fail rules for this step, e.g. "p99 < 1s".

Step.description: One HTTP request in a scenario.

url.description: URL of the system under test, for reports. Requests go to the step URLs.

idle_timeout.description: How long an idle keep-alive connection stays open, e.g. "30s".

base_url.description:
Base URL that step URLs starting with "/" are appended to. An absolute
http(s) URL or a ${variable}, without a query string or fragment.

expr.description:
Threshold expression: a metric, an operator and a value, e.g.
"p95 < 500ms" or "error_rate < 1%".

abort_on_fail.description:
Stop the test when the threshold fails. Accepted by the format;
whether an engine acts on it depends on the engine release.

delay_abort.description:
Defers the abort: abort checks for this threshold start this long
after the run starts, e.g. "30s" (Go duration syntax, like the other
durations). The threshold is still evaluated during the delay and
still decides the final verdict; only the abort is deferred. The
engine defines the exact run-start clock. Requires abort_on_fail.

Threshold.description: A pass/fail rule: an expression such as "p95 < 500ms", or an object with the expression and abort settings.

virtual_users.description:
Constant load: number of virtual users (at least 1). Use instead of
stages.

duration.description:
Constant load: how long the test runs, e.g. "5m". Leave it out to have
each virtual user run its scenario once.

ramp_up.description: Constant load: time to start all virtual users, e.g. "30s".

stages.description:
Staged load: each stage moves to its target number of virtual users
over its duration. Use instead of virtual_users, duration and ramp_up.

http_timeout.description: Timeout for each HTTP request, e.g. "30s".

scenarios.description: Scenarios that virtual users run, picked at random by weight.

region_config.description: Share of the virtual users per cloud region.

thresholds.description:
Pass/fail rules for the whole test, e.g. "p95 < 500ms" or
"error_rate < 1%".

expected_statuses.description:
HTTP status codes (100-599) that count as a successful request, for
steps without a status check whose on_fail is fail or abort; such a
check decides for its own step instead. Leave it out (or write []) to
use the engine's default.

title: VoltTest test definition
description: A VoltTest load test: the load profile, the system under test and the scenarios that virtual users run.
